label: 噬根巨龙 burrow
subject: An ancient WINGLESS black root-gnawing dragon, long low reptilian body, four strong clawed legs, tapering curled tail, ridged charcoal scales with rotting dark green gaps, crooked horns, earthy worn teeth. No full wings, no giant fire breath or glowing aura. A long predatory muzzle facing right and compact curved tail to fit square frame. Body length more prominent than height.
prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Animate EXACTLY the project character in input1. Retain every identifying feature and the exact anatomy, scale, colors, material, body proportions, equipment and camera angle of the reference. Four BURROWING poses on one fixed invisible ground line:1 full dragon crouches head-first toward ground;2 head and forequarters sink below ground with back/tail still visible;3 only curved hind-back and upright tail remain;4 only a small tail tip above the same ground line. This is intentional progressive disappearance, not shrinking the creature. Preserve scale, no ground tile, hole ring, dirt cloud, rubble, effects or background.
Keep the dragon WINGLESS, four-legged, long low black body, dark green scale gaps, curled tail, same horn count and long snout. Do not make it a biped or add wings.
Layout: EXACTLY FOUR frames in a2by2equal-cell grid, all cells equal192x192logicalpixels, reading order left-to-right then top-to-bottom. TWOlogicalpixelclearborder around EVERY cell, no cropped horns, tail, fingers or robe. Common exact scale and fixed foot ground line at logical y189. Ground line is fixed; visible amount changes intentionally, but do not scale the whole creature smaller.
Use exact limited reference RGBpalette, crisp low-resolution pixelart, upper-left light, dark outlines, no dithering or smooth shading. True transparent background, binary alpha, no frame lines, label, name, text, watermark, cast ground shadow, scene, root, stone, effect, smoke, poison cloud, spell circle, particle or aura.

postprocess.operation: remove isolated crop-boundary alpha fragment from neighboring cell, whole-frame placement
